title: State and event reference
text:
State
Accepted lifecycle events / completion




idle
CONFIGURE → configured


configured
CONNECT → initializing; RESET → idle


initializing
Successful initialization → connected


connected
QUERY.EXECUTE; TRANSACTION.BEGIN → transaction.begin; DISCONNECT → disconnected


transaction
See substates below; completion → connected


disconnected
Terminates DuckDB, then → configured


error
RESET → configured; current initialization failures do not transition here



Transaction substates are begin, within_transaction, execute, commit, rollback, end, and error. Only within_transaction accepts execute, commit, and rollback events. A successful execute returns there; successful commit or rollback reaches end and returns the root to connected.
RECONNECT and CLOSE exist in the exported event union but have no handlers. Use the supported disconnect/connect sequence instead.

title: State and event reference
text:
Configuration and connection payloads
CONFIGURE takes config: MachineConfig, containing dbInitParams: DuckDBConfig | null, dbLogLevel: LogLevel, and tableDefinitions: TableDefinition[].
CONNECT takes dbProgressHandler and statusHandler; both can be null. Status callbacks report initialization progress and readiness. The status type includes error, but initialization does not currently invoke that status on rejection.
QUERY.EXECUTE and TRANSACTION.EXECUTE take queryParams: QueryDbParams. See Queries for result options. Catalog events are forwarded to the child actor; root snapshot.can() for a catalog event does not guarantee the child is ready to perform that operation.

title: State and event reference
text:
Error behavior
The current machine does not provide uniform recovery. Initialization and some child actor failures can error the actor rather than reach root error. A transaction query/commit/rollback failure enters transaction.error, which has no external recovery event. Observe actor errors, use timeouts, and dispose of the database before creating a replacement actor. The demo can be restarted by reloading its frame.
Catalog load callbacks have inconsistent error shapes on some paths: do not assume the first callback argument is always a successful instance name. Inspect the catalog’s error context and validate success before querying a returned name.

title: Optimistic projections
text: These optional helpers generate SQL for local changes layered over an authoritative table. They do not send requests or synchronize with a server; your application owns acknowledgement, rejection, and incoming snapshots.

title: Optimistic projections
text:
Lifecycle

createOptimisticOperationsTableSql() creates the operation ledger.
createOptimisticOperationBeginSql({ changeSetId, entityId, fields }) records local values in committing state.
createOptimisticOverlayViewSql({ entityColumn, fields, sourceTable, viewName }) creates a view that applies the latest local value per entity and field.
On acknowledgement, use createOptimisticOperationAckSql({ changeSetId, committedAt, operations }); on an ambiguous result use createOptimisticOperationUnknownSql(changeSetId); on rejection use createOptimisticOperationRejectSql(changeSetId).
After a new authoritative snapshot arrives, createOptimisticOperationReconcileSql({ entityColumn, fields, metadataColumn, sourceTable }) removes local fields whose source metadata matches their change-set ID.

All SQL builders return strings; execute them using a DuckDB connection. executeOptimisticOperation(connection, action, sql) wraps execution with telemetry. hasOptimisticChangeSet(connection, { changeSetId }) checks whether ledger entries remain.

DuckDB, driven by state
text:
@jr200-labs/xstate-duckdb manages a browser DuckDB database with XState v5 actors. Configure a database, run SQL, coordinate transactions, and load versioned tables through typed events.
Get started Try the live demo

title: DuckDB, driven by state
text:
What it provides

A database lifecycle machine with observable connection and transaction states.
Queries returning Arrow tables, arrays, maps, or scalar values.
A table catalog with Arrow IPC loading, version retention, and subscriptions.
Load metrics, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and SQL helpers for optimistic projections.

title: DuckDB, driven by state
text:
How it fits together
Your application sends events to duckdbMachine. The root actor manages the database and transactions; its dbCatalog child manages table definitions, queued loads, versions, and subscriptions. DuckDB-Wasm executes SQL in a browser worker.
The library does not provide a database server or durable synchronization. The demo uses an in-memory database that is recreated when the page reloads. DuckDB worker and WASM assets are fetched from jsDelivr during connection.
The documentation and demo are built from the same repository revision. See the API reference for supported events and the live demo to watch state transitions.

title: Live demo
text:
Configure → Connect → Run query. DuckDB runs in your browser; reloading starts a new session. Open full screen.

How to use the demo

SQL query: run SQL directly, or begin a transaction, execute, and commit or roll back. Wait for each operation to finish.
Table catalog: subscribe, then load the supplied Arrow sample. List tables to find the physical table name to query.
Configuration: edit the sample YAML before configuring. Disconnect and reset to configure again.
Output / State details: open a side panel for event history, actor context, and load metrics. Close it to give the editor more space.

The compact diagram shows root transitions; the state badge includes transaction substates. DuckDB assets download from jsDelivr on connection. If an operation fails, reload to restart; see error behavior.

title: Table catalog
text:
Include definitions in the root CONFIGURE event’s config.tableDefinitions:
const tableDefinitions = [{
  schema: 'main',
  name: 'measurements',
  isVersioned: true,
  maxVersions: 2,
}]
A versioned load creates a new physical table and retains up to maxVersions. Use callback or subscription instance names when querying; the logical specification name is not the versioned physical name. Loads are queued and processed by the catalog actor.

title: Table catalog
text:
Load data
After connecting, send a data object inside CATALOG.LOAD_TABLE:
database.send({
  type: 'CATALOG.LOAD_TABLE',
  data: {
    tableSpecName: 'measurements',
    tablePayload: compressedArrowBase64,
    payloadType: 'b64ipc',
    payloadCompression: 'zlib',
    callback: (instance, error) => console.log(instance, error),
  },
})
Pass a base64 Arrow IPC string and set payloadCompression to 'zlib' or 'none' to match its encoding. The demo includes a compressed Arrow sample.
payloadType: 'json' is present in the public type, but its current loader only records metrics and does not insert data into DuckDB. Use Arrow IPC for actual table loading. The demo disables JSON loading until the library implements it.

title: Table catalog
Table catalog
text:
Inspect the catalog
database.send({ type: 'CATALOG.LIST_TABLES', callback: console.log })
database.send({ type: 'CATALOG.LIST_DEFINITIONS', callback: console.log })
The catalog snapshot is available from database.getSnapshot().children.dbCatalog. Its context contains loadedVersions, subscriptions, pendingTableLoads, loadMetrics, and error. The package exports DuckDbCatalogSnapshot for typed access.
CATALOG.DROP_TABLE is declared as an event but its current handler does not implement removal. Do not depend on it for cleanup; disconnect to terminate the demo database, or manage physical tables explicitly using SQL and account for catalog metadata yourself.

title: Getting started
text:
Install the library and its peer dependencies in your browser application:
pnpm add @jr200-labs/xstate-duckdb xstate @duckdb/duckdb-wasm apache-arrow @opentelemetry/api @opentelemetry/api-logs
The current library requires DuckDB-Wasm >=1.33.1-dev42.0 <2, Arrow >=21 <22, OpenTelemetry API ^1.9.1, and OpenTelemetry Logs API ^0.221.0. For React, also install @xstate/react.

title: Getting started
Getting started
text:
React
Use const [snapshot, send, actor] = useActor(duckdbMachine) from @xstate/react. Send the same events as above and disable controls with snapshot.can(event). The demo shows a complete React integration, including the catalog child snapshot.

title: Getting started
text:
Cleanup
When finished with outstanding queries and transactions, send DISCONNECT while connected. Wait for configured before stopping the actor so the asynchronous DuckDB termination can finish:
database.send({ type: 'DISCONNECT' })
await waitFor(database, state => state.matches('configured'))
database.stop()

title: Getting started
text:
Run these docs locally
Use Node.js 22 or newer, the pnpm version declared in package.json, and Quarto.
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm docs:preview
Quarto’s pre-render hook installs locked workspace dependencies, builds the library, and builds docs/demo into docs/demo-assets. Quarto copies that bundle into _site. For faster demo-only development, run pnpm demo:dev. Run pnpm docs:build for a production site.

title: Observability
text:
The catalog context’s loadMetrics tracks cumulative encodedBytes, decodedBytes, and loadedBytes, with a byTable breakdown keyed by table specification name. These measure payload processing, not the live DuckDB heap size. Pruning older versions does not subtract historical load counts.
Send CATALOG.METRICS.RESET_LOADS to reset all totals, or include tableSpecName to reset just one table’s contribution. Exported helpers are createEmptyDuckDbLoadMetrics, recordDuckDbLoadMetric, resetDuckDbLoadMetrics, and duckDbLoadMetricByteLength. Types are DuckDbLoadMetrics, DuckDbLoadMetricBucket, and DuckDbLoadMetricRecord.

title: Observability
text:
OpenTelemetry
The consumer supplies the OpenTelemetry API and Logs API peer dependencies and configures providers and exporters appropriate for its runtime. Without registered providers, instrumentation is a no-op. The demo does not configure a telemetry exporter.







Span
Operation




xstate.duckdb.init
Engine initialization; includes duckdb.version


xstate.duckdb.close
Engine termination


xstate.duckdb.query
Query; description, result type and row count


xstate.duckdb.tx.begin
Begin transaction


xstate.duckdb.tx.commit
Commit transaction


xstate.duckdb.tx.rollback
Roll back transaction


xstate.duckdb.load_table
Load; table, payload type/compression and instance


xstate.duckdb.prune
Version pruning


xstate.duckdb.optimistic_operation
Local operation action and outcome



Optimistic operations also emit xstate.duckdb.optimistic.operation.count, xstate.duckdb.optimistic.operation.duration (milliseconds), and a trace-correlated structured log. Their attributes contain action and outcome, not SQL or field values.
Other database operations record exceptions and an xstate.duckdb.error event on failure. Exception messages may contain database details; configure exporters according to your application’s requirements.

title: Queries and transactions
text:
Send QUERY.EXECUTE while the root is connected. Supply queryParams with sql, description, resultOptions, and an optional callback. Each query actor acquires a connection and runs independently; do not assume two consecutive sends will finish in order.
database.send({
  type: 'QUERY.EXECUTE',
  queryParams: {
    description: 'grouped-values',
    sql: "SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('a', 1), ('a', 2)) AS t(category, amount)",
    resultOptions: { type: 'multimap', key: 'category', value: 'amount' },
    callback: result => console.log(result), // Map { 'a' => [1, 2] }
  },
})










resultOptions.type
Additional options
Result




array
None
Array of Arrow row objects


arrow
None
Apache Arrow Table


dictionary
key
Map of key to row; later duplicate keys replace earlier rows


multimap
key, optional value
Map of key to arrays of rows, or projected values


singlevaluemap
key, value
Map of key to one projected value


firstvalue
key
First row’s named field, or null


firstrow
None
First row, or null



Use unique SQL aliases when joining tables: duplicate output column names are rejected. Multimap keys must be truthy; a missing key, empty string, zero, or false raises an error.

title: Queries and transactions
text:
Transactions
Transaction events are asynchronous. Wait for transaction.within_transaction after beginning and after every execution, then commit or roll back. The following continues with the database actor from Getting started:
import { waitFor } from 'xstate'

database.send({ type: 'TRANSACTION.BEGIN' })
await waitFor(database, s => s.matches({ transaction: 'within_transaction' }))

database.send({
  type: 'TRANSACTION.EXECUTE',
  queryParams: {
    description: 'create-example',
    sql: 'CREATE TABLE measurements (value DOUBLE)',
    resultOptions: { type: 'array' },
  },
})
await waitFor(database, s => s.matches({ transaction: 'within_transaction' }))

database.send({ type: 'TRANSACTION.COMMIT' })
await waitFor(database, s => s.matches('connected'))
Use TRANSACTION.ROLLBACK instead of commit to discard changes. Auto-commit queries are not accepted while the root is in a transaction. Set suitable waitFor timeouts and handle failures in production code.
